### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Lowry-Wood syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.790)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:34016)

**Proposed mechanism:** RNU4ATAC (HGNC:34016) —DISRUPTS→ U12-dependent splicing (GO:0000394); U12-dependent splicing (GO:0000394) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); U12-dependent splicing (GO:0000394) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002650); U12-dependent splicing (GO:0000394) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); U12-dependent splicing (GO:0000394) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004325). Mutations in RNU4ATAC disrupt the U12-dependent spliceosome, a critical component of the splicing machinery. This disruption leads to aberrant splicing of numerous genes, manifesting as microcephaly, skeletal dysplasia, intellectual disability, and short stature, which are common phenotypes in both primordial dwarfism and Lowry-Wood syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in RNU4ATAC with distinct functional consequences (e.g., gain-of-function for one disease and loss-of-function for the other) or the discovery of distinct critical downstream pathways affected by RNU4ATAC mutations in each disease. _(variant: The presence of common benign variants in RNU4ATAC in the gnomAD database that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of RNU4ATAC in U12-dependent splicing provides a common therapeutic target for both microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type I and Lowry-Wood syndrome. Strategies aimed at restoring spliceosome function or compensating for its defects could benefit patients with either condition.
